faqs.q: Do LeavesOut gutter guards work against heavy Henderson County pine needles?
faqs.a: Yes, absolutely. Henderson County is famous for dense stands of Eastern White Pine whose long, slender needles clog traditional wire mesh and perforated screens. LeavesOut features a solid aluminum, nose-forward curved hood with zero openings on top. Water adheres to the curve via surface tension and enters the gutter, while pine needles cannot make the curve and fall harmlessly to the ground.

faqs.q: What communities in and around Hendersonville does Cory Rose service?
faqs.a: Cory Rose and LeavesOut of the Blue Ridge provide full installation and maintenance throughout Hendersonville, Flat Rock, Mills River, Laurel Park, Fletcher, Etowah, Horse Shoe, Balfour, Mountain Home, Dana, Edneyville, Saluda, Tuxedo, Zirconia, Brevard, and South Asheville/Arden.

faqs.q: Will installing LeavesOut gutter guards void my existing roof warranty?
faqs.a: No. Unlike older gutter covers that nail directly into or under your roof shingles (which can void manufacturer shingle warranties), LeavesOut is engineered to mount securely directly to your fascia board or gutter lip with heavy-duty patented brackets. Your shingles remain completely untouched and fully protected.

faqs.q: How does LeavesOut handle heavy mountain downpours in Western NC?
faqs.a: LeavesOut is lab-tested and field-proven to handle over 11 inches of rainfall per hour—far exceeding even the most intense tropical storm downpours ever recorded in the Blue Ridge Mountains. The patented surface tension design channels 100% of water directly into the downspouts.

faqs.q: Is the Lifetime No-Clog Warranty transferable if I sell my Hendersonville home?
faqs.a: Yes! The LeavesOut Lifetime No-Clog Warranty transfers seamlessly to the next homeowner. If your gutters ever clog with LeavesOut installed, Cory Rose will come out and clean or service them completely free of charge.

faqs.q: Do you match my home's trim and gutter colors?
faqs.a: Yes. LeavesOut comes in over 20 baked-on enamel colors—including dark bronze, musket brown, forest green, clay, white, and copper penny—to match your existing roofline, fascia trim, or custom siding seamlessly.

faqs.q: Why is excavating on the Cashiers-Highlands Plateau different from lowland grading?
faqs.a: The Plateau averages 3,500 to 4,500 feet in elevation and receives up to 80-100 inches of rainfall annually—among the highest rainfall totals in the continental US. Excavating here requires specialized understanding of mountain hydrology, steep slope stabilization, and Blue Ridge granite mechanics. Good excavation channels water safely away from foundations without causing erosion or runoff into local waterways.

faqs.q: How does Joel Rice handle solid granite bedrock on a building site?
faqs.a: We operate heavy commercial excavators fitted with high-frequency hydraulic rock breakers. Rather than expensive and disruptive blasting, we mechanically fracture and extract granite bedrock to exact footing depths, keeping your pad level and structurally sound.

faqs.q: How does Joel Rice ensure fair, upfront pricing without hidden surprises?
faqs.a: As the longest single-owned and operating excavation contractor on the Plateau (over 35 years), Joel Rice visits every jobsite personally. We provide honest upfront estimates, assess rock risks in advance, and recommend money-saving adjustments to your site plan while refusing to cut corners on structural integrity.

faqs.q: Can you handle septic tank excavation and perk failure remediation?
faqs.a: Yes. We excavate certified residential and commercial septic systems, shallow-placement drain fields, and advanced engineered mound systems across Jackson and Macon counties, working directly with county health inspectors.

faqs.a: Call Joel Rice directly at (828) 743-5801 or visit our shop at 327 Hunter Road in Cashiers. We provide prompt on-site consultations across Cashiers, Highlands, Sapphire, Glenville, and Lake Toxaway.
